title: High availability with multiple AZs and Regions

kcs.statement: Running an application's resources in at least two Availability Zones keeps it available when one AZ fails, and is the standard way to achieve high availability within a Region.
A second Region is used for disaster recovery from a Region-wide outage, for lower latency to users on another continent, or to meet residency rules in several countries.
Multi-Region designs add cost and complexity (cross-Region replication and data transfer), so multi-AZ is the default for availability and multi-Region is chosen only when a requirement demands it.

problem_ideas: A web shop runs two EC2 instances, both in eu-west-1a: what single change gives high availability?
